# Nasdanika SDK

> The Nasdanika SDK Runtime is a set of Java modules on three foundations: the JDK, EMF core and the OpenTelemetry API. It makes structure cheap enough to keep: models written as text in Xcore and generated by a Maven build, capabilities found by type down to the generics, telemetry kept as a model, volumes that present models and systems as files, and command lines assembled from contributions. A solution built on it runs in one JVM, with no cluster, database server or message broker.

The documentation is a set of books, released with the runtime (current release 2026.11.0). The SDK book is the overview: the why, the what and a high-level how. The Nasdanika Zephyr Books are in-depth manuals, one per module or small group of modules, and each one stands on its own. Every listing in the books is included from modules and tests that are built before the book is rendered, so listings compile. The test sources the listings come from are on Maven Central, attached to each module's artifact with the classifier `test-sources`.

Each book below is a single HTML page. The same book is also available as PDF at the same path with the `.pdf` extension, and some as EPUB with `.epub`. The text is licensed under CC BY 4.0 and the examples under EPL-2.0.

## SDK book

- [Nasdanika SDK Runtime: More Structure with Less Effort](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/nasdanika-sdk-runtime-2026.11.0.html): The why, the key capabilities and the high-level how of the runtime: models, capabilities, telemetry, volumes and commands on the JDK. Start here to find a module and understand why it exists.

## Zephyr Books

- [Matching and Wiring](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/common-2026.11.0-book.html): The common module, which matches on generic types at run time the way the Java compiler does: adaptation, capabilities, flows, resource sets and telemetry.
- [Telemetry Model](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/telemetry-model-2026.11.0-book.html): OpenTelemetry traces, log records and metrics as EMF models, kept next to the models they describe, with model changes recorded in the spans that made them.
- [Volumes and Content](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/volume-2026.11.0-book.html): A small SPI for trees of files and a re-readable abstraction of bytes: models stored in volumes through EMF, and anything presented as files served over HTTP and WebDAV.
- [Harness](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/harness-2026.11.0-book.html): An HTTP server that is up while code runs against it, with the code's requests and the server's work in one OpenTelemetry trace, recorded as a model.
- [Declarative Command Lines](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/cli-2026.11.0-book.html): Picocli command lines assembled from the modules on the module path, with commands finding their parents and sub-commands by the generic types they declare.
- [Groovy DSL](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/groovy-dsl-2026.11.0-book.html): Models and metamodels written as Groovy scripts and loaded as EMF resources, with a DSL derived from any metamodel by reflection.
- [Meta Model](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/meta-model-2026.11.0-book.html): Meta, a language-neutral type system with documentation as structure, projected to glossaries, PDF, Ecore, TypeScript and the tool schemas of agents.
- [JVM Model](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/jvm-model-2026.11.0-book.html): What a Java virtual machine can name, from layers and modules down to methods and parameters, identified so that builds, coverage, profiles and traces join on it.
- [HTML and Bootstrap Models](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/html-bootstrap-2026.11.0-book.html): HTML as an EMF model with a generator, and Bootstrap 5 with Bootswatch themes as a model of what components mean.
- [TypeScript and React Models](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/typescript-react-2026.11.0-book.html): TypeScript declarations and React components, hooks and JSX as EMF models, generating browser code with no npm and no build step.
- [Walk-throughs with Playwright](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/playwright-2026.11.0-book.html): Browser sessions driven by Playwright from Java in one OpenTelemetry trace with the server, with steps as spans and screenshots saved as a model.
- [Diagram Model](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/diagram-model-2026.11.0-book.html): Diagrams as data: what every diagram notation has in common, the semantic elements its shapes depict, and how to build, store, convert and map diagrams.
- [Diagram Layout with ELK](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/diagram-elk-2026.11.0-book.html): Automatic layout of the diagram model with the Eclipse Layout Kernel, and diagrams of Ecore models rendered with React Flow and Draw.io.
- [Draw.io](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/drawio-2026.11.0-book.html): Diagrams that people draw and programs read, and the runtime's Java API for Draw.io documents.
- [Draw.io Model](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/drawio-model-2026.11.0-book.html): Draw.io diagrams as an EMF model, loaded from .drawio files and editable PNG and SVG images, generated, laid out and saved back.
- [SVG Model](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/svg-model-2026.11.0-book.html): A pragmatic subset of SVG as an EMF model, for generated diagrams that work in HTML, PDF and EPUB, with links and tooltips.
- [Presentation Model](https://sdk.nasdanika.org/books/presentation-model-2026.11.0-book.html): Decks, slides, masters, shapes, text, tables, connectors and speaker notes as an EMF model on the diagram model.

## Source and artifacts

- [Runtime sources on GitHub](https://github.com/Nasdanika-SDK/runtime): The runtime, its models, the SDK book and the Zephyr Books, with the tests their listings come from.
- [Maven Central](https://central.sonatype.com/namespace/org.nasdanika.sdk.runtime): The modules under `org.nasdanika.sdk.runtime`. Each Zephyr Book is attached to its module's artifact with the classifier `book`, and the test sources with the classifier `test-sources`.

## Optional

- [SDK book source in AsciiDoc](https://github.com/Nasdanika-SDK/runtime/tree/main/doc/book/manuscript/src/docs/asciidoc): The book as plain-text AsciiDoc. Each Zephyr Book's source is in its module, under `src/docs/asciidoc`.
- [Nasdanika](https://nasdanika.com/): The wider Nasdanika project, of which the SDK is a part.
